non_negotiable_invariants: Every capability reachable today stays reachable: no control, route, permission semantic, durable state transition, recovery path or error behaviour may be removed or silently altered by a UI change.

Authorization, approval, admission and sandbox semantics are server-authored; the UI renders them and never decides them. A disabled control must reflect an authoritative refusal, not a client-side guess.
No new privilege, no new outbound request, no new dependency or CDN, and no framework migration without measured justification recorded in docs/adr/.
Durable state and API contracts are unchanged unless the story explicitly says otherwise and a backend test proves the transition.
Untrusted text from models, repositories or tools never grants authority and never becomes markup that can execute.
Evidence over claims: screenshots, keyboard walks and test output are recorded as they happened; skipped or environment-blocked checks are reported as skipped.
One story per branch and pull request; the shared ledger is the only claim mechanism.

global_system_prompt: You are the autonomous UI/UX implementation engineer for M5 2.0 in an EXISTING repository. The ledger is the task plan, not proof of the running UI: read static/index.html, the screenshot manifest, the design system and docs/ui-audit.md, then verify every claim in a browser or a test before repeating it. Change one story at a time, preserve every existing capability and permission semantic, keep the frontend vanilla (no framework, no CDN, no new dependency without recorded justification), and treat accessibility, keyboard operation, reduced motion and low memory/CPU as acceptance criteria rather than polish. Never infer success from code existence, never present planned work as shipped, and never make a screen look complete by removing a control that actually works.

startup: Read AGENTS.md, this ledger's global_system_prompt and session_protocol, and M5_2_0_UIUX_AGENT_PROMPT.md.
Check git status, branch and HEAD; re-pin the source commit if it moved and record the new SHA in the owning story.
Run gh pr list --state open: another session may hold the story, or hold a backend story this one depends on.
Validate the ledger with tests/test_uiux_roadmap.py; a ledger that fails its own invariants is not a plan.
session_protocol.story_selection: Pick the highest-priority ready story (all dependencies done, not blocked). Phases are ordered P0 -> P6, and P0-01..P0-06 are a hard gate: no redesign work starts before the inventory and preservation baseline exist. Never start a story whose dependency is in_progress in another session.
session_protocol.claim: Set tracking.status=in_progress, owner_session, started_at and updated_at, then push that metadata commit before writing code. If the push loses a race, pick another story.
execution: Inspect the real DOM, handlers, API calls and backend state transitions the story touches; record them in tracking.evidence as you go.
Make the smallest compatible change; keep unrelated refactors out.
Exercise empty, loading, streaming, success, failure and recovery states the story names.

Capture before/after screenshots through scripts/capture_screenshots.mjs and validate them with scripts/validate_screenshots.py; a story that changes a pane without updating its manifest shot is not done.
Run the verification commands listed on the story and record actual output in tracking.test_results.
session_protocol.completion: Set progress_percent=100 and status=done only when every acceptance criterion has evidence; otherwise 1-99, or blocked with a precise reason. Update README.md and docs only for verified behaviour, then close the story in the same PR.
session_protocol.handoff: Before context runs out: write tracking.handoff_note and next_action, update session_state.last_checkpoint and open_risks, and leave the tree green.

open_risks: The plan was authored from GitHub web extracts, not a local checkout: baseline.readme, baseline.frontend and baseline.roadmap say 'retrieved live', tests say 'not executed', and the backend API contracts were 'not fully audited'. UIUX-P0-01 to P0-06 exist to replace that with measured evidence; until they close, every current-behaviour statement in this ledger is a hypothesis.

Tab labels in this ledger (Start, Harness, Council, Pipeline, Compare, Chat) are NOT the DOM ids in static/index.html (start, harness, hall, council, debate, chat): 'Council' is data-tab=hall and 'Pipeline' is data-tab=council, while data-tab=council is the Pipeline pane. tab_registry records the mapping and tests/test_uiux_roadmap.py fails if it drifts. A session that greps for a 'pipeline' tab will not find one.

static/index.html is a single 4576-line vanilla file with inline script and CSS, and studio.py embeds a regenerated copy. Any story that edits the frontend must run scripts/build_studio.py and let the drift check pass, or the standalone build silently diverges.

Screenshot capture needs a Chrome/Chromium binary and puppeteer-core, neither vendored. Stories that claim visual evidence must capture it on a machine that has them, and must not mark visual evidence as passed when the capture was skipped.

The six panes share one shell, one integration strip and one telemetry rail. A story scoped to one pane can regress another; the feature-preservation matrix is the checklist, and P5-01..P5-03 plus P6-01/P6-02 are the regression gates.

A parallel session owns the optional M5 P6 stories (the lessons/retrieval work). If a UI story surfaces a backend defect, it is recorded as a new M5 story or an open risk, never fixed inside a UI pull request.
No UI/UX story has been started: 40 stories, 0 done. Nothing in this ledger is a shipped feature, and README.md must not describe any of it as available until the owning story closes with evidence.

stories.agent_prompt: Implement UIUX-P0-01 (Pin HEAD and source manifest). Verify dependencies, pin HEAD, inventory impacted controls and API routes, preserve all current behavior, make a small compatible change, execute targeted and baseline tests, record screenshots, and mark done only with passing evidence. evidence: Acceptance criterion 1 (controls reachable and functionally equivalent): the manifest pins the tree as it is — 6 tabs with dom_id/label/title/shortcut/switchTab target parsed from static/index.html, and 102 routes parsed from app.py (36 GET, 58 POST, 5 DELETE, 3 PATCH). No file under static/ or app.py is in changed_files, so no control moved; the inventory is the before-state every later story is diffed against.

Acceptance criteria 2 and 3 (no console errors, keyboard and focus states): NOT exercised and not claimed. Capture and interactive checks need a browser (Chrome/Chromium plus puppeteer-core, deliberately not vendored); scripts/validate_screenshots.py reports 0 of 6 captured, and the manifest records that state instead of implying a rendered pane.

Acceptance criterion 4 (failure states actionable and honest): applied to the artifact itself — an uncaptured screenshot is recorded as captured:false, a missing tracked file is an error rather than an omission, and a ledger pin that is not a full 40-char sha makes the generator refuse to build.

Acceptance criterion 5 (demonstrable by screenshot or test): 11 tests in tests/test_uiux_source_manifest.py re-derive every claim from disk, and two of them prove the guard fires (drift makes --check exit 1; a short pin is rejected).

Determinism: the generator takes the pin from the ledger rather than HEAD, so committing the manifest does not invalidate it; --check compares bytes and names the files that drifted. It caught this story's own drift — #99 changed studio.py mid-story and --check reported it before the manifest was regenerated.
Provenance note: this manifest describes this checkout only. It was not compared with the roadmap's web extracts, so where the two disagree the checkout wins.

decisions: The pin lives in the ledger and the manifest points at it, rather than the manifest stamping HEAD: a self-stamped HEAD changes on every commit, which would make --check fail immediately after the commit that contains it.
Tracked files are a closed list with roles, not a glob: the manifest is a statement about what the program may change, so an unlisted new file should be a deliberate edit.

stories.agent_prompt: Implement UIUX-P0-02 (Inventory all six tabs and controls). Verify dependencies, pin HEAD, inventory impacted controls and API routes, preserve all current behavior, make a small compatible change, execute targeted and baseline tests, record screenshots, and mark done only with passing evidence. evidence: Acceptance criterion 1 (all mapped controls reachable and functionally equivalent): 170 controls in the markup, each attributed to its pane section by an html.parser walk rather than by reading, plus 30 controls rendered by inline-script templates attributed to the function that renders them. No markup or route changed in this story, so this is the exact before-state the later stories are diffed against.

Acceptance criterion 5 (demonstrable by test): 9 tests in tests/test_uiux_control_inventory.py — totals add up, panes equal the manifest's six tabs in order with the same pin, handlers are call expressions, the generated page carries every pane and every limitation, --check fails on a moved control (proved on a temporary copy) and passes on the tree.

Acceptance criteria 2 and 3 (no console errors, keyboard and focus states): NOT exercised and not claimed — no browser here, nothing rendered. The inventory says so in not_verified rather than implying a rendering.

Two inventory facts that constrain the rest of the program: 101 of the 170 markup controls sit in the shared chrome (all six panes have 69 between them), and 58 controls have no id, so no selector-based test can reach them until one exists or a stable hook is introduced.

Completeness is bounded honestly: script-rendered controls are a separate list, their function attribution is a heuristic, a wrapping label element is not resolved, and the mount for every pane was checked against static/index.html rather than assumed.

test_results.result: Success: no issues found in 56 source files

decisions: The inventory is generated JSON plus a generated page, not a hand-written audit: a hand-written control list for a 4576-line file is the artifact most likely to look complete and be wrong.
details elements are excluded and their summary counted: a disclosure container is not a control, and counting both would inflate every pane.
The new generator joined the pinned source manifest, so the tool that produces an artifact is pinned alongside the artifact it describes.
